candidate_label: Discrete solid nodule separated from pleural boundaries
description: A compact, rounded to mildly lobulated solid nodule with a clearly outlined margin, surrounded by aerated lung rather than broadly merging with pleural, chest-wall, mediastinal, or diaphragmatic soft tissue. It remains visible as a discrete soft-tissue opacity on mediastinal windows; nearby thin vessels may touch it, but there is no broad soft-tissue attachment.

candidate_label: Discrete solid nodule surrounded by aerated lung
description: A compact solid nodule lies within aerated lung, with dark lung separating it from the chest wall, mediastinum and diaphragm across the three views; thin vessel connections may be present. Its outline is usually rounded or oval, unlike the low-response examples that broadly abut or merge with a pleural or diaphragmatic soft-tissue boundary.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule separated from pleura by aerated lung
description: A compact, rounded to mildly lobulated nodule is surrounded by aerated lung, with a visible lung gap between it and any nearby pleural or chest-wall surface rather than broad attachment or blending into that surface. Small vessels or short strands may touch its margins, but the nodular body remains distinct.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule separated from the pleural surface
description: A compact, rounded or mildly irregular nodule lies within aerated lung, with a visible lung gap separating it from the chest wall, diaphragm, or other broad soft-tissue boundary. Fine vessel connections or short radiating strands may be present, but the opacity is not predominantly a flat band or a broad-based projection from the lung boundary.

candidate_label: Discrete solid nodule separated from pleural soft tissue
description: A discrete, predominantly solid nodule is surrounded by aerated lung, with an intervening lung gap where the pleura or chest wall is nearby rather than a broad attachment to pleural or basal soft tissue. Its solid body remains visible on mediastinal windows and does not blend into a hazy peripheral opacity or broad linear band.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule with surrounding aerated lung
description: A compact soft-tissue-density nodule is set within dark aerated lung, with a visible lung gap separating most of its contour from the chest wall, diaphragm, or other broad soft-tissue boundary. Thin vessel-like attachments or short pointed extensions may be present, but the nodule does not broadly merge into a nearby surface.

candidate_label: Compact nodule with an aerated-lung border (nonspecific)
description: The high examples generally show a discrete, rounded or lobulated nodule with aerated lung directly bordering its anterior or free lung-facing edge, sometimes with a fine adjoining linear opacity. However, several low examples have the same visible configuration, so it does not consistently distinguish the groups.

candidate_label: Rounded nodule with an exposed anterior margin
description: A discrete, bulky round-to-ovoid opacity has a convex anterior-facing border against darker aerated lung, visible at the top of the axial image and left of the sagittal image. It remains nodular across planes rather than becoming a thin band, elongated branching structure, or broad sheet continuous with the chest wall; its other borders may be irregular or touch the pleura.

candidate_label: Nodule separated from pleural boundaries
description: A compact rounded, ovoid or mildly lobulated nodular opacity surrounded by aerated lung, without visible contact with the pleura, chest wall or diaphragmatic boundary. Small vessels or fine strands may approach its margins, but the opacity remains distinct from a broad peripheral soft-tissue boundary.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule surrounded by aerated lung
description: The nodule forms a compact round, oval, or short triangular opacity within aerated lung, with a visible dark lung gap separating it from the pleura or chest wall in all three planes. It is not broadly continuous with a pleural surface or predominantly part of a long linear band.

candidate_label: Aerated-lung nodule interface without pleural contact
description: The nodule is surrounded by aerated lung rather than broadly abutting a pleural or mediastinal soft-tissue boundary. Fine vessel-like lines or short strands commonly approach or merge with its margins; a nearby pleural surface, when visible, remains separated by aerated lung.

candidate_label: Nodule surrounded by aerated lung
description: The nodule sits within the lung, with a visible dark lung gap separating it from the chest wall, mediastinum, and diaphragm across the three views. Thin vessels or strands may contact it, but it does not merge directly into a broad bright pleural or soft-tissue boundary.

candidate_label: Lung-surrounded nodule with adjacent fine strands
description: A tentative pattern is a nodule largely separated from pleural or mediastinal soft tissue by aerated lung, with fine linear or branching densities approaching its margins. The nodule itself may be solid and smooth or hazy and irregular; neither appearance consistently distinguishes the groups.

candidate_label: Nodule with a mostly aerated lung surround
description: The nodule is a discrete rounded or irregular opacity with dark aerated lung around most of its margin, sometimes crossed by thin linear strands or vessels. It is generally not broadly merged with the chest wall, diaphragm, or mediastinal soft tissue.

candidate_label: Compact non-pleural nodule beside small vessels
description: A compact rounded, oval, or mildly lobulated opacity with a dense centre, separated from the pleura by aerated lung. Small branching vessels lie immediately beside it or appear to meet its margins, sometimes forming short linear extensions.

candidate_label: Nodule separated from pleural surfaces
description: The focal opacity lies within aerated lung, with a substantial dark lung gap—typically about 10 mm or more—between it and the chest wall or diaphragm in the three views. Unlike many L examples, it is not touching or immediately adjacent to a broad pleural surface.

candidate_label: Compact solid lobulated nodule with an aerated lower border
description: A bulky, rounded-to-lobulated nodule remains predominantly soft-tissue dense on mediastinal windows, with an inferior solid contour bordering aerated lung and often bearing short irregular projections or strands. Small internal air spaces may occur, but the opacity is not mainly ground glass, an air-filled lesion with a thin rim, or an elongated pleural band.

candidate_label: Bulky solid nodule with a defined lower edge
description: A compact, rounded or lobulated opacity has a substantial continuous soft-tissue-density component that remains visible on the mediastinal window, with a distinct lower edge against dark lung on coronal and sagittal views. Small internal air spaces or radiating strands may be present, but the opacity is not mainly a thin-walled air space, faint haze, or a narrow band.

candidate_label: Air-surrounded solid nodule margin
description: A predominantly solid nodule, or a thick soft-tissue wall around an air space, has an outer contour bordered mostly by aerated lung rather than broadly merging with pleural, chest-wall, or mediastinal soft tissue. Thin vessels or strands may join the margin; a broad attachment to an adjacent soft-tissue surface is absent.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule bordered by aerated lung
description: The nodule or thick-walled ring is a distinct opacity with dark aerated lung around most of its outer contour, rather than broadly merging with the chest wall, mediastinum, or another large dense structure. Thin vessel-like or linear connections may be present, but they do not obscure most of the nodule boundary.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule outlined by aerated lung
description: A discrete soft-tissue nodule or thick-walled cavitary nodule is bordered predominantly by aerated lung, rather than broadly merging with pleural, diaphragmatic, or chest-wall soft tissue. Small branching vessels or short tapering strands commonly meet its margin. A nearby pleural surface may be present, but an intervening gap of aerated lung is usually visible.

candidate_label: Anterior nodule margin with a projecting strand
description: The nodule, or its thick wall, has an anterior-facing margin that tapers into a point or a short linear strand extending into dark, aerated lung—toward the top of the axial image and the left of the sagittal image. This margin is typically angular or irregular rather than smoothly rounded or broadly continuous with the chest wall.

candidate_label: No consistent visible discriminator
description: Both groups contain solid rounded or lobulated nodules, irregular hazy opacities, and flattened pleural-based opacities. Pleural proximity or attachment, adjacent branching vessels, indistinct margins, and internal air lucencies do not consistently separate the groups.

candidate_label: No consistent visible discriminator
description: Both groups contain peripheral nodules, including rounded dense nodules, irregular or branching opacities, and nodules touching or connected to the pleural surface. Neither pleural proximity, margin shape, nor persistence on the mediastinal window consistently separates the groups.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule surrounded by aerated lung
description: A distinct rounded or lobulated nodular opacity lies within aerated lung, with a visible lung gap separating it from the pleura, chest wall, diaphragm, and central soft tissues. Small vessels or thin strands may contact its margins, but it does not broadly merge with an adjacent dense tissue boundary.

candidate_label: Discrete nodule surrounded by aerated lung
description: A distinct rounded, ring-shaped, or irregular nodular opacity lies within the lung, with dark aerated lung separating its main body from the pleura, chest wall, and mediastinum. Thin vessel-like or spiky extensions may enter the nodule, but it is not broadly merged with an adjacent soft-tissue boundary.

candidate_label: Hazy nodule with a small denser core
description: The nodule has heterogeneous attenuation, with a hazy or indistinct lower-density periphery and a relatively small denser centre. Much of its lung-window footprint becomes inconspicuous on mediastinal windows, unlike a uniformly solid, well-defined soft-tissue nodule.

candidate_label: Hazy nodule with a small dense core
description: The nodule has a hazy, fluffy or finely irregular outer component surrounding a brighter central focus, rather than being uniformly dense with a sharp border. Much of its visible extent on the lung window disappears on the mediastinal window, leaving only a small faint or irregular central remnant.

candidate_label: Juxtadiaphragmatic or cardiac-border lung
description: The nodule lies immediately above or against the curved diaphragm, or along the cardiac/mediastinal border, with adjacent aerated lung containing fine vascular markings. Proximity to these broad soft-tissue boundaries, rather than proximity to the lateral chest wall alone, is the distinguishing pattern; nodule shape and density vary.

candidate_label: Basal lung beside the diaphragmatic dome
description: The nodule lies in a basal wedge or crescent of lung immediately above a broad, smooth, domed soft-tissue boundary, most clearly seen in the coronal and sagittal views. This lung often tapers toward a corner beside the chest wall or heart; the shared pattern is the surrounding basal anatomy rather than a particular nodule shape or density.

candidate_label: Compact rounded solid nodule with a free lung margin
description: A compact, round-to-oval solid nodule with a predominantly smooth or gently lobulated, sharply defined border against aerated lung. Aerated lung separates it from the pleura or diaphragm, rather than the nodule having a broad surface attachment or blending into branching or bandlike soft tissue.

candidate_label: Compact, rounded solid nodule with a clear lung interface
description: The nodule is a compact round or oval opacity with predominantly smooth, convex, sharply defined borders and a solid core that remains visible on the mediastinal window. Dark aerated lung outlines most of its circumference, unlike the predominantly flattened, branching, ill-defined, or broadly pleural-attached opacities in the L images.

candidate_label: Bulky solid opacity with an irregular lung-facing edge
description: High examples usually show a substantial, predominantly soft-tissue-density opacity that remains conspicuous on mediastinal windows, with a lobulated or irregular lung-facing margin and short projections or adjoining linear strands. Low examples more often appear predominantly hazy, thin-walled around an air space, or flattened and bandlike rather than thick and solid.

candidate_label: Solid opacity with a sharply defined lung-facing border
description: A dense, largely filled-in opacity remains conspicuous on the mediastinal window and has an abrupt border against dark lung, often with a convex, lobulated, or pointed upper contour. Compared with this pattern, most L images show a faint hazy opacity, a thin elongated band, or an air-containing center rather than a substantial solid body.

candidate_label: Discrete solid nodule surrounded by aerated lung
description: A compact, round-to-oval solid nodule with a smooth to mildly lobulated, clearly defined border against aerated lung and a substantial soft-tissue core on mediastinal windows. Aerated lung separates it from the pleural, diaphragmatic, and mediastinal surfaces; small vessels may touch it, but its outline remains distinct rather than blending into branching or hazy opacities.

candidate_label: Compact, rounded solid nodule surrounded by lung
description: A discrete, compact round-to-oval nodule has a mostly smooth, sharply defined convex outline and a solid centre that remains visible on the mediastinal window. Aerated lung separates it from the pleura or other broad soft-tissue surfaces, although a thin vessel may touch it; it is not predominantly streak-like, branching, or broadly pleural-attached.

candidate_label: Discrete rounded solid nodule in aerated lung
description: A compact, round-to-oval, fairly homogeneous solid-appearing nodule with a well-defined, smooth to mildly lobulated outline. Aerated lung separates it from nearby pleural, diaphragmatic or mediastinal soft tissue, even when the nodule is peripheral; it is not a flattened pleural opacity or an ill-defined patch of ground-glass density.

candidate_label: Compact, well-defined solid round nodule
description: A discrete round or mildly oval bright nodule has a compact, largely uniform solid centre that remains visible on the mediastinal window, with a fairly sharp border against surrounding dark lung. It retains a rounded or mildly lobulated shape across the three planes rather than appearing predominantly hazy, band-like, branching, or broadly merged with the pleura or diaphragm.

candidate_label: Discrete solid nodule surrounded by aerated lung
description: A discrete, relatively homogeneous solid nodule with a mostly defined contour and aerated lung around it, including separation from the pleura and diaphragm. candidate_label: Discrete solid nodule away from pleural surfaces
description: A compact, round-to-oval solid opacity lies within aerated lung, with roughly a nodule-width or more of lung separating it from the nearest pleural, chest-wall, or diaphragmatic surface. Unlike most L examples, it is not immediately subpleural or merged with a broad surface-based opacity.

candidate_label: Boundary-adjacent nodular and linear opacity
description: An irregular or elongated soft-tissue opacity lies against, or only a short distance from, a pleural, diaphragmatic, or mediastinal surface. Its margins often blend into tapering strands or a broader band extending through the intervening lung or along that surface, rather than forming an isolated rounded nodule.

candidate_label: Pleural-connected, bandlike or tented opacity
description: The nodule or opacity is continuous with a nearby pleural surface or fissure, either through a broad attachment or through conspicuous linear bands. Its outline often has a tapered, triangular or tented extension rather than appearing as an isolated compact round nodule.

candidate_label: Possible discrete solid nodule in aerated lung
description: High examples usually show a compact, fairly homogeneous solid nodule with a smooth to mildly lobulated outline, separated from the pleura by aerated lung, often with a fine vessel approaching its margin. However, several low examples have the same visible appearance, so this is only a tendency rather than a reliable distinguishing pattern.

candidate_label: Discrete rounded focus with surrounding air
description: The H images generally show a compact, rounded or oval bright focus with a clearly defined convex border and dark aerated lung around most of its perimeter. In contrast, many L targets lie directly against the pleural surface or merge into a larger central or branching opacity, rather than appearing as a discrete intrapulmonary focus.

candidate_label: Solid nodular tissue merging with branching strands
description: The opacity usually has a substantial solid core or thick soft-tissue rim, with lobulated or angular margins that merge directly into several branching vessels or linear strands. This connected, branching contour is more typical of the high examples than a hazy opacity or a smooth, relatively isolated peripheral nodule.

candidate_label: Dense, sharply outlined angular margins
description: A dense white opacity has an abrupt border against dark lung, with angular shoulders, pointed extensions, or junctions with thick linear structures rather than a uniformly smooth, rounded outline. The dense portion remains conspicuous on the mediastinal window; in hollow lesions, this appearance is found along a thick, uneven wall.

candidate_label: No consistent distinguishing CT pattern
description: Both groups contain small, rounded solid-appearing nodules in aerated lung, as well as larger or irregular opacities with adjacent linear structures. Margin sharpness, ground-glass density, proximity to the pleura, and nearby vessels do not consistently separate the groups.

candidate_label: No consistent visible CT pattern
description: The H images include small rounded dots, larger solid-appearing nodules, a ring-shaped opacity with a dark centre, and irregular patchy opacities. Nodule density, edge shape, and proximity to the pleura overlap substantially with the L images, without a consistent visible separator.
